title: The vision model that answered unknown
blurb: Timeouts returned a fake prediction instead of a downgrade.
prompt: A pipeline consumed thousands of unknown labels as real classifications after a model timeout, because the draft returned them with a 200 and no provenance. The same draft dereferenced caller-supplied object URLs. Review it, fix it, and prove degradation is explicit and references are scoped.
aiNote: The draft maps model timeouts to a successful prediction of unknown with no provenance marker, so downstream consumers train on fabricated labels, and it fetches whatever object URL a caller supplies rather than enforcing the tenant storage prefix.
testIdea: Force a timeout and assert the response marks the downgrade or fails, never a default label as a normal prediction; submit a foreign URL and assert 403 before the fetch; assert a result names the exact model version.
followUps: Which failures should downgrade and which should fail the request?
How would you expire results without losing auditability of decisions made from them?
What confidence signal would you surface for a downgraded result?
